verdict.rationale: Better Auth is code-first with no dashboard ('No dashboard clicks'). Its functionality, including admin operations, is exposed through server-side auth.api methods and HTTP endpoints, and the openAPI() plugin generates a schema covering core and plugin endpoints. However, the plugin is self-described as early-stage, no explicit API/UI parity statement exists, and a hands-on report says the request-header-based design made admin scripts and tests hacky. missing for 10: explicit documented parity guarantee, a mature (non-early-stage) OpenAPI surface, frictionless headless/scripted admin use, independent corroboration of full programmatic coverage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: No dashboard clicks. Your auth lives in code version controlled, type-safe, and reviewable in PRs.
To authenticate a user on the server, you can use the `auth.api` methods.
Better Auth's openAPI() plugin generates an OpenAPI 3.1.1 schema covering core and plugin endpoints
It allows administrators to perform various operations such as creating users, managing user roles, banning/unbanning users, impersonating users, and more.
